newsitem.title: USA: Md. lawmakers sign last-minute budget measures.
newsitem.headline: Md. lawmakers sign last-minute budget measures.

text.p: Maryland Gov. Parris Glendening will sign hundreds of new laws today, including several key spending bills passed as the General Assembly's 1997 expired at midnight Monday.

During the final hours of the legislature, lawmakers passed a plan to limit economic growth in rural areas. The plan backed by Glendening funnels development into areas where roads and utilities are already in place.
In addition, a bill is awaiting Glendening's signature that will provide $254 million to the Baltimore school system.
But some city officials opposed the bill's provision granting the state more control of the district.
City Council President Lawrence Bell called the measure a betrayal and says it takes control of the schools away from the city and puts it in the hands of the Governor and state Board of Education.
